theorem_title: Each explicit sensor-kernel witness has nonzero target
natural_language_statement:
For $n\in\mathbb N$ and $x=(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb Z^2$, define the observation $r_n(x)=x_1+(n+1)x_2$, target $q(x)=x_1$, and witness $w_n=(n+1,-1)$.

$$
q(w_n)\ne0\qquad(n\in\mathbb N).
$$

This gives the nonvanishing-target component of the explicit blindness witness. The separate kernel identity identifies the associated observation that vanishes.
formal_statement:
theorem NewMathDiscovery.LinearBlindness.RankTwoInstability.target_nonzero_on_witness (n : Nat) :
    target (witness n) ≠ 0 := by sorry
